chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'If a person in ihram kills game, he said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said, 'And if he repeats?' He said: 'Upon him, every time he repeats, an expiation.'

key_terms.عَ: Abbreviation for 'Alayhi al-Salam' (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing game while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the cumulative nature of the expiation (kaffarah) for hunting while in ihram, establishing that each distinct act of killing game incurs a separate penalty. It reflects the juristic principle of individual accountability for repeated violations of the sacred restrictions during pilgrimage, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity of the Haram boundaries.
